decision: Owner decision, ledger 2409, option 2 of issue old-oracle-project-number-in-public-files: mask the number in the tracked tree and rebind the evidence; the history is not rewritten.
digestRule: A recorded digest that pinned a changed file follows the file: a 64-hex string that was the sha256 of a changed file's bytes, or the sha256 of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII or UTF-8 or default separators) of a changed JSON file or of any sub-value of it, is replaced by the digest of the new value, repeated until no digest changes. A digest that pins the bytes a file had in git at a recorded commit (recorderInputs, probeInputs: checked with git show <commit>:<path>) is not rewritten, because that history is unchanged. spec/compatibility/history-rewrite-2026-09-28.json is a record of a past rewrite and is left byte for byte.

rule: Every occurrence of the twelve-digit number in a tracked text file is replaced by the placeholder, byte for byte, with nothing else changed. The placeholder is the one the Auth, Identity Platform and Storage sandbox fixtures already use for their own project numbers. Replays of a masked fixture compare the placeholder with the placeholder; no judge or comparer depends on the literal number. The twelve-digit number was never inside a longer digit run in a tracked file, and no base64 or varint encoding of it was found (docs.local/tools/scan-encoded-numbers on the parent tree).
subject: The project number of the retired production oracle project fireemu-35fe6. The project id stays: it is an identifier of a project that is not secret and the issue names only the number.
verification: preSha256 of every entry is the sha256 of the file at parentCommit (git show parentCommit:path). postSha256 is the sha256 of the file in the commit that carries this version of the record and in every later commit that does not touch the file.

Rebuilding a file: take the bytes at parentCommit; at each maskedOffsets entry (a byte position in those bytes, ascending, each the start of a whole 12-digit run) put the placeholder in place of the 12 digits; then replace every old digest of digestRewrites by its new one at the same time (each old digest is present in the masked bytes, each pair is two 64-hex strings). The result must equal the file byte for byte. Entries marked editedAfterCascade also carry a hand edit (see handEdits) and cannot be rebuilt this way.

Restoring the old bytes: put every new digest back to its old one, then put the old number back at each offset in ascending order (an offset is the position in the restored bytes). The result has sha256 preSha256. Only someone who holds the number can do the last step.

tools/compat-history/history.py pins this record by sha256 (REBIND_RECORD_SHA256) and compares a frozen corpus with its anchor by rebuilding each named file as described above. A frozen file may differ from the anchor only by those substitutions. postSha256 is not used there. Entries for files outside the frozen sets are inert.

tools/ci/test_project_number_positions.py is a backstop, not the exact check: it fails if a 10 to 13 digit number is written in a project-number position of a tracked text file (projects/<digits>, <digits>-compute@, service-<digits>@, gcf bucket names, acat.p2-<digits>, NUMBER constants, projectNumber / project number, project_id, project <digits>, user-project, or a project id followed by a number) unless it is the placeholder or a listed made-up number. A number written in another way passes it. Exact-match detection is done by the local pre-commit and pre-push hooks (which read the real numbers from untracked local sources) and by docs.local/tools/scan-encoded-numbers. The guard also keeps every listed made-up number at least 3 digits away from the real numbers wherever those local sources exist.
